session_start.dispatcher: main process startup only; async Agent launch path is N5/MC and has no second session.start dispatcher call
session_start.fixture_guard: module-scoped spawnedOnce; set before agent.spawn; later same-module session.start invocation returns next(event)

stream_order.row: ContentBlockStop yields a completed assistant row with current block, outer UUID, timestamp, and API block index before message_delta/message_stop.
stream_order.terminal_row_metadata: The producer resets wp per response, pushes every completed content-block row into wp, then on message_delta updates usage and terminal fields by iterating every row in wp; it is not limited to the last row.
order: on generator resume, the query stores X=eo??M and enqueues X tool_use blocks into streamingToolExecutor
executor invokes W1 with the stop-time assistant row separately from the pre-query ToolUseContext.messages snapshot
stream_order.append_result: Ui.appended awaits append side effects but returns no accepted replacement row; the query uses its native raw/projection row for tool enqueue. This is the pinned Native behavior.
stream_order.next_request_history: The selected query row X=eo??M is pushed to K. At the next turn boundary H.messages is [...w,...K,...je]; the next round derives w from H.messages and passes its prompt-built Zt.messages to callModel. The session.append projection result is not assigned into K/H. Normal next-round history preparation can still transform those rows.
stream_order.sibling_context: sameTurnToolUses contains prior sibling blocks in the executor only; the current block is a separate W1 argument and later sibling blocks are not included.
stream_order.live_tool_settlement: After each stream event the query polls Tn, which emits completed results without waiting for unfinished tools; the final getRemainingResults wait occurs after the API stream loop. Executor context layers can update its internal context on completion, while query-local he adopts newContext from the final drain before PostToolBatch.

jsonl_persistence.path_scope: The TS recorder below is the headless turn-consumer path. The interactive transcript UI has a separate MSe/ASe recorder; it uses the same NE/transcript-writer path, but not TS.record().
jsonl_persistence.assistant_row_recording: With persistSession enabled, the headless consumer pushes each assistant row into its current transcript and calls TS.record() immediately on row arrival, after the query append side effect. That call is not awaited. Default record() selects all currently present rows: its default ge=false makes ANt(...,!ge) return the full list, including an assistant row whose stop_reason is still null. The TS cursor advances before NE() is called; the later message_delta record call does not select the same row again.
jsonl_persistence.query_append_scope: The main query wraps Xl in Ui.through (also through the observer wrapper). Ui.R accepts uuid/type rows of type user, assistant, attachment, or system and calls Xq when session.append is enabled and the running conversation is hookable. Thus the Tn user/tool-result row also passes through session.append before it is yielded to the headless consumer. Ui.through awaits that side effect, then yields the original event value; the hook projection is not substituted into the query event. The explicit r.appended(M) call remains a separate assistant-tool-use path, with Ui deduplicating the same row through its WeakSet.
jsonl_persistence.live_tool_result_recording: A tool_result is delivered as a user row. After Ui.through has completed the session.append side effect and yielded the original row, the headless user-row branch pushes it into the current transcript, awaits TS.record(), and only then continues consuming the stream. Therefore a completed tool result may be persisted while the provider stream is still open; the writer receives the original Native tool-result row, not the session.append projection.
jsonl_persistence.writer_path: TS.record() calls NE(), which normalizes the selected rows and invokes mi().insertMessageChain(). The writer awaits session-message reads, creates an outer transcript envelope by spreading each source row, then appendEntry enqueues that entry. The per-file queue preserves FIFO after admission; drain serializes with LM(entry) and appends the serialized chunk. Its scheduled flush interval is 100 ms.
jsonl_persistence.snapshot_limit: Static source proves an early write attempt, not whether its eventual JSONL bytes contain stop_reason:null or the terminal value. The row unwrap and transcript envelope are shallow spreads that preserve the nested message object; MessageDelta later mutates that same message object in the parser. Because the assistant record is not awaited and JSONL serialization happens later in the queue drain, either snapshot can win. The assistant and tool-result insertions also have async reads before queue admission, so this source alone does not guarantee their queue-admission order across separate record calls.
jsonl_persistence.interactive_cutoff: The interactive MSe.write path calls the same NE writer but passes isResponseInFlight to ANt. While that flag is true, ANt stops before the first assistant row whose stop_reason is null, so the incomplete trailing assistant row is held out of the persisted slice. ASe invokes MSe.record from transcript-snapshot and response-state effects. This pins the in-flight cutoff, not the precise scheduler moment when a post-delta row is flushed.
jsonl_persistence.tombstone_path: The headless tombstone branch calls TS.evict(message.uuid). If that row has passed the record cursor, TS.evict requests removeMessageByUuid; accepted fallback tombstones can therefore remove an already-recorded discarded assistant row. This does not establish that every error/decline path tombstones every earlier row.

stream_error.disposition: A final thrown model-stream error with no fallback-chain target reaches the model-error finalizer.
stream_error.completed_tools: The finalizer emits already completed results, takes any remaining finished results, and records ordinary user/tool-result rows.
stream_error.in_flight_tools: It discards the executor, aborts executing tools, leaves queued tasks unstarted, rebuilds the executor, and emits removals for in-progress IDs.
stream_error.unmatched_uses: It emits a synthetic cancelled tool_result for each remaining unpaired tool_use; the cancellation text warns that already-started effects may have happened.
stream_error.retry: This finalizer does not keep tool executions live for a model retry. A separate fallback-chain attempt uses abandonAttempt and its own tombstone/reset/abort path.

server_fallback.scope: The allowlist decline is inside the server_fallback event branch and runs only when the projection is userVisible; the target check is uA(toModel) ?? (Ur(toModel) || ay(toModel)).
server_fallback.prior_results: je aliases ue.toolResults. Rows already handed off by earlier per-event Tn polls live in je; when a normal poll yields a result, xr appends its projected user rows after the yielded event is resumed. xr also preserves attachment rows and user rows returned by the normal tool-result projection. A tool that completed after the previous poll is not proven to be in je yet.
server_fallback.decline: The branch snapshots We = je.slice(), then ue.reset({clearAssistantMessages:false}) clears the original je array. After pruning K only for discarded assistant UUIDs and rows whose message.model equals toModel, it tombstones those K rows and every row in We, removes in-progress tool IDs, appends the synthetic decline assistant row, pushes that same row into K, yields it, and breaks out of the event loop. Decline tombstones do not carry displayOnly.
server_fallback.accepted: The accepted branch always prunes K by M.discardedMessages UUID. It clears no je entries unless tombstonedToolUse is true; in that case to=[...je] snapshots every current result/attachment entry, reset empties je, the executor is discarded/rebuilt, and every row in to is tombstoned with displayOnly:true. If tombstonedToolUse is false, je remains intact. This is whole-attempt je cleanup, not a filter by discarded tool IDs.
server_fallback.ordinary_abandon: abandonAttempt is a separate cleanup: it tombstones all current assistantMessages and toolResults, then reset(clearAssistantMessages:true); do not infer this broader cleanup for server_fallback.

synthetic_decline_row.refusal_call: $dt('refusal', {type:'refusal', category:M.apiRefusalCategory??null, explanation:null, fallback_credit_token:null, fallback_has_prefill_claim:null, recommended_model:null}, M.requestId, ge)
synthetic_decline_row.refusal_result: Native refusal helper returns an assistant API-error row with error=invalid_request, requestId from the event, stop_reason=refusal, and stop_details equal to the refusal metadata; it is not an SDK LlmError. The helper generates its own default timestamp/UUIDs and refusal-facing text.
synthetic_decline_row.other_reason_call: cs({content:"The server routed this response to a model that is not in your organization’s availableModels allowlist; the response was discarded.", error:"invalid_request", now:B.now, uuid:B.uuid})
synthetic_decline_row.other_reason_result: The generic Native cs/Dyn constructor returns an assistant row with isApiErrorMessage=true, error=invalid_request, one text block, native model xa, stop_reason=stop_sequence, empty stop_sequence, default usage, outer timestamp from B.now(), and separate generated outer uuid/message.id.
synthetic_decline_row.append_and_yield: If the helper returns a row, r.appended(Ro) is awaited first; then the exact Ro row is pushed into K and yielded.

server_fallback.tombstone_consumers: Accepted fallback sets displayOnly:true on both discarded assistant rows and every je entry copied into to. The generic event dispatcher passes only e.message to the callback, dropping displayOnly. The headless consumer calls xr.evict(message.uuid) without a displayOnly check; the interactive callback removes by UUID and calls xNt, which calls removeMessageByUuid. MSe/ASe are snapshot recorders, not the tombstone deletion gate.
server_fallback.flow_boundary: The decline break and accepted continue bypass the common per-event yield*Tn() at the bottom of the stream loop. The sa wrapper finally calls the underlying iterator.return() but ignores its return value and emits no finally event; any underlying cleanup side effects remain outside this source claim.

concurrency_cap.parser: finite integer environment parser; invalid or <1 values are undefined and therefore use 10; no upper clamp.

clock_sleep.validation: finite non-negative milliseconds; cancellation signal is forwarded to clock.sleep
clock_sleep.local_stub_wait: Node setTimeout only delays the loopback child response; it does not emulate Native clock.sleep.
